title: Marble Runs & Ramps
strapline: Higher, steeper, faster — will it reach the bottom?
intent: Ramps and runs are cause-and-effect made visible: change the slope and the ball changes, so children can genuinely experiment.
Building a run that works is real engineering — connecting, aligning, adjusting until the marble makes it all the way.
It is naturally full of early physics talk — faster, slower, steeper, higher, further — and prediction.
The instant, repeatable feedback (it works, or it doesn't) drives children to test, tweak and try again.
Working out a shared run together is genuine collaboration and problem-solving.
implementation: Offer open-ended materials — guttering, tubes, cardboard, blocks, crates — plus balls of different sizes and weights.
Let children build and fail and rebuild; resist making a working run for them to copy.
Wonder aloud to nudge thinking: 'It stopped halfway — I wonder what would make it keep going.'
Feed in the language of what's happening: steeper, faster, higher, gap, join, slope.
Set gentle challenges: get the ball to travel further, or slower, or to land in the bucket.
Encourage comparing and predicting: which ball rolls faster, which ramp is steeper.
Take it outside and big — down slopes, off crates, along fences — for whole-body versions.
key_questions: Why do you think the marble stopped there?
What could you change to make it go faster — or slower?
How can we join these pieces so there isn't a gap?
Which ramp is steeper — how can we tell?
How will you get the ball to land in the bucket at the end?

impact.text: Children build and connect ramps and runs, solving how to align the pieces so the ball travels the whole way.
Children experiment with slope, height and different balls, and predict and explain what will happen.
Children compare speed, steepness and distance using early physics vocabulary.
Children test, adjust and rebuild persistently, driven by the run either working or not.
Children work together on a shared run, sharing ideas and materials to make it work.
Children talk through their plans and reasoning as they build and improve the run.

enhancements: Lengths of guttering, tubes, kitchen roll centres and cardboard channels.
Balls of different sizes and weights, and things that don't roll well to compare.
Blocks, crates and tape for building supports at different heights.
Buckets, funnels and targets to aim the marble into.
A big outdoor version down a slope or off crates.
Water added to the runs for a different flow to investigate.

playing_exploring: Children experiment freely, testing how slope, height and different balls change what happens.
They take the risk of a run that might not work, and enjoy finding out.
active_learning: Children stay with the tinkering, rebuilding again and again until the marble makes it.
creating_thinking: Children predict, test and explain cause and effect, and adjust their design to solve the problem.
